Median ask − median bid

MapleStory Market’s published hourly chat/megaphone medians. Spread = seller median − buyer median; percentage spread divides that difference by their midpoint. Only matching source/hour pairs are compared; missing sides stay missing. This is a difference between offer medians, not an executable order-book spread, profit opportunity, or evidence of a completed sale. Offers never enter MPI or the cash-item sale estimate.

Prices of cash items, with fixed weights.

This experimental index weights known-price cash items by their qualifying reference-week estimated meso expenditure. Membership, base prices and capped expenditure weights stay fixed. Daily prices need at least five recorded sales; missing observations carry forward only after a qualifying price has been observed. Incomplete initial priced coverage stays blank.

Cash indexₜ = 100 × Σ fixed cash weightᵢ × meso priceᵢ,ₜ / base meso priceᵢ

A cash price index measures cash-item meso price changes with fixed base weights. The NX exchange-rate estimate divides cash-item meso prices by fixed NX purchase costs and uses changing daily recorded-volume weights. Their percentages measure different things. Neither changes the existing NX headline or the non-cash basket.

Why can’t the rolling capture use a custom lookback?
The captured scanner supplies one median and one item-specific window per item. These cash-item windows span 3–30 days; there is no underlying daily scanner history here to reconstruct other windows. Source-input backlog: dated historical captures or a documented lookback query, with window bounds, recorded volumes, sold-price basis and timestamps, would be needed before enabling custom rolling windows. No new query or connected source is implied.
Single-item NX prices from the documented Cash Shop schedule; bundles, crate cosmetics, expired offers and unknown purchase prices are excluded. Recheck this schedule when Nexon changes prices. Each daily rate weights the item’s meso/NX ratio by that day’s recorded sale volume.

OPEN METHODOLOGY
Show the work.
A useful market measure starts with knowing what is being measured.
What is the reference week?
The fixed reference period is : the initial seven source-calendar dates beginning with Grand Launch on October 21. This project chose that dated opening period as a reproducible starting point. These are calendar-day aggregates, not seven full 24-hour intervals from an exact opening hour; 18:00 UTC is the separately announced Founder’s Access time, not an established Grand Launch time.
For MPI and Cash Basket, 100 represents the basket at its reference prices; individual days in that week need not equal 100. NX percentage change compares with its frozen reference-week rate. The versioned baseline stays fixed: there is no arbitrary week chooser that could silently rebase or drift it. The 48h, 7d and Founders controls change chart views only. The pricing table’s source-calendar lookback changes its cash-item estimates only; it changes neither the baseline nor the headline.
Each category dial uses that category’s reference-price mix on those same dates, rather than the whole 50-item basket. Its arc fills from 0 to the needle on a shared scale. Category average weight is total category basket weight divided by its item count; individual item weights can differ.
A basket based on spending why 50?
Basket v2 freezes the 50 non-cash items with the largest estimated meso turnover in : daily median price × recorded sold volume. Eligibility requires at least five reference days with recorded volume of 50 or more. For eligible items, all reference days with at least five recorded sales enter the base calculations. These counts do not establish stack quantities or independent traders.
Base price is the sale-volume-weighted average of daily medians in that reference week. Base spending is that price multiplied by recorded base sale volume. Weights are spending shares, capped at 8% with excess redistributed until all weights sum to 100%. Thus a cheap ore with many sales and an expensive scroll with fewer sales both contribute in proportion to estimated mesos spent. The cap applies to base weights; a large later price change can still have a larger effect.
This v2 history is reconstructed using a fixed basket selected later. It is separate from the earlier count-selected v1 series, whose definition and published values remain archived. An index change caused by switching definitions is not a new market move.
MPIₜ = 100 × Σ wᵢ × (priceᵢ,ₜ / base priceᵢ)wᵢ ∝ base priceᵢ × base sale volumeᵢ · max 8%
Daily medians × sold volume approximate turnover; they do not equal an exact transaction-value sum. The source does not expose the underlying stack-level trades here. There is no claim to measure total meso supply. Clean and upgraded equipment can mix in aggregate medians, introducing quality/composition bias.
Launch context on charts
Nexon announced Founder’s Access for October 6, 2026 at 11 AM PDT (18:00 UTC), and Grand Launch for October 21, 2026. The Grand Launch time is not established here. Chart markers show these calendar days; daily aggregates retain their source-day boundaries and cannot identify prices before or after an intraday opening. Founders period means October 6–20 inclusive; Grand Launch onward begins October 21. All-time charts may extend the axis to October 6 when the first recorded point is October 7; no observation is added. Nexon launch announcements via Steam ↗
Can turnover reveal total meso circulation?
Turnover is a flow over a period; meso balances are a stock at a moment. The same coins can fund repeated purchases, while stored or inactive balances remain unseen. This feed does not measure money creation (faucets), destruction (sinks) or how often money changes hands (velocity). Consequently, these data identify neither total meso supply nor a defensible confidence interval. Estimating supply would require independent balance coverage and validated measurements or assumptions about those missing quantities; no numerical estimate is published.
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics, UK Office for National Statistics and Statistics Canada weight consumer-price baskets by household spending. Keeping a reference mix stable helps distinguish price changes from changing purchases; agencies periodically refresh baskets and adjust for quality. Their detailed formulas differ: this project borrows the basket principle, not national CPI coverage. Sources: BLS, ONS, Statistics Canada.
Here, estimated meso turnover replaces household spending. This fixed 50-item basket measures selected game-market prices, not a player's cost of living. Liquidity screens, base-weight caps and dated coverage disclosures improve reproducibility, but cannot establish complete coverage or manipulation immunity. Cash Shop items are excluded to separate ordinary meso-goods prices from NX conversion and monetized-item supply; this is the project’s analytical scope choice. NX's percentage change uses cash-item ratios with changing daily volume weights; MPI uses fixed base-expenditure weights, so the two measure different things.
  • Strength: a stable, inspectable basket makes price comparisons reproducible without silently changing what the index tracks.
  • Limits: players substitute, gear quality varies, new items arrive, and supply unlocks move prices; incomplete coverage remains.
Why 50 items?
Fifty is this project’s initial, inspectable market basket size, not a U.S. CPI rule or a statistical guarantee. It focuses on regularly traded items with usable reference-week observations. The coverage below shows how much activity it captures; excluded items and changes in item quality can behave differently.
Membership stays fixed between explicit basket versions. I review broader coverage and category concentration separately; adding items would create a new version and preserve this history. Recorded sale counts are not independent-trader sample sizes, and a larger count alone does not establish accuracy.
What counts as evidence?
Shop observations→Source-inferred sales→Daily medians + volume
These are scanner-derived sale estimates rather than user-entered asks. The source’s underlying scanner may infer a sale when a shop closes and an item is gone. A disappearing listing or a grey row is evidence with limitations; neither independently proves a trade. I do not classify an item as sold merely from its sprite color.
Using a fixed basket, sale-volume-weighted prices and capped spending shares makes a single posted quote less influential after this site is published. Smega asks and player reports never enter the MPI; these choices reduce manipulation risk, while coordinated trades, wash trading and scanner errors can still distort observed sales.
Asking prices, signed-in player reports, and smega advertisements are separate signals. They are labeled and plotted separately when observations are available. Missing series stay empty instead of inventing history.
How this compares with the US CPI
Shared principleWeight price changes by spending in a reference basket.
This indexVirtual items, one-week base, market medians, fixed item mix, no seasonal or quality adjustment.
US CPIHousehold expenditure weights; modified Laspeyres aggregation, geometric means in many lower-level categories, and quality adjustments.
The cap, narrow market coverage, short base period and game-specific supply shifts make this a commodity-style market index, rather than a household cost-of-living index. BLS methodology ↗

HONEST FRESHNESS
More polls ≠ more trades.
The collector checks every 10 minutes. When upstream data changes, all calculations and charts refresh together. A daily feed remains daily data, even if checked frequently.
Intraday scanner inputs require timestamps, sold evidence and coverage thresholds. Below 80% MPI basket weight or 60% NX volume across three cash items, the corresponding headline stays on the daily snapshot.

SOURCE HEALTH / PROVENANCE
Always know how old it is.
Market observation time, source publication time, and this site’s check time are different clocks.
Green: healthy within the stated clock’s scope.Amber: delayed, dated capture or no qualified live feed.Red: failed check or stale/missing source.Daily-source age bands: up to 36h / 36–72h / over 72h. Collector-check bands: up to 30 min / 30–180 min / over 180 min. These are this site’s display thresholds, not provider guarantees. Capture times never establish fresh trades.
What happens when something breaks?
The collector keeps the last valid feed when an upstream request fails. Malformed data and overlapping collectors cannot replace it. Every snapshot preserves its original source time. Source age and collector health are shown separately: daily-source age uses 36/72-hour bands, while collector checks use 30/180-minute bands and failed checks turn red immediately. Failed checks mark retained daily data amber unless its source time is already over 72 hours old or missing. Missing daily time is red; a missing check time is amber unless the check failed. Qualified intraday input is green only when under 40 minutes old and otherwise amber; older or absent intraday input alone does not turn the status red.
Your open tab checks a small version file about once a minute while visible, with jitter and backoff. Prices are fetched once by the collector, never per visitor. Charts and tables use the same versioned payload.
